newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK commemorates dead Chinese democracy activists.
newsitem.headline: HK commemorates dead Chinese democracy activists.

text.p: Groups of pro-democracy campaigners demonstrated in Hong Kong on Saturday to demand the release of Chinese dissidents jailed in China and to commemorate activists killed in democratic movements.

"Release democracy campaigners," about 20 protesters chanted as they marched to China's diplomatic mission, the local branch of the Xinhua News Agency, on the annual Qingming Festival when Chinese honour dead relatives and friends.

They laid wreaths at the building's entrance to salute Chinese demonstrators killed in the 1989 student-led democracy movement centred on Beijing's Tiananmen Square when China sent tanks to crush their protests.
The Hong Kong activists also burned two paper doves to protest at the lack of freedom in China.
China has jailed or exiled most of its small band of active political dissidents.

To honour those killed in the 1989 protests, other Hong Kong campaigners laid flowers and wreaths on Saturday before a replica of the white Goddess of Democracy statue built by the Chinese students in the Tiananmen Square movement.
Many people in Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 after more than 150 years as a British colony, worry about China's refusal to countenance democratic reforms.
